answers.question: Question 14: You said that after a refund call times out, the agent "retries once, then re-reads the order and refund records and reports what it finds". The rule now re-reads only when the second call also gets no answer. I propose changing it. Before: "When the second refund call also got no answer, the agent re-reads the refund before it reports the refund's state." After: "After a refund call that timed out, the agent sends it once more and then re-reads the order and its refund, whatever the second call answered, and reports what the re-read shows."
answers.recommended: Yes, change the rule to the "After" text.
answers.reply:
> 3. Cancel succeeded, refund call timed out — state unknown; agent retries once, then re-reads the order and refund records and reports what it finds. Final message must match the final refund status.
> For case 3, after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: pending or issued, report that status; failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet; re-read fails, say status unknown and hand off.

answers.question: Question 15: You said reads (the order list, a re-read of the order or its refund) "may be retried on timeout without limit". Nothing then ends a read that keeps getting no answer, and the agent could keep the customer waiting for ever. I propose a new rule. Before: (no rule) After: "When a read of the customer's orders, or a re-read of an order or its refund, gets no answer, the agent tries it again up to two more times. After the third try with no answer, it acts as the rules say for a read with no answer."
answers.recommended: Yes, add the rule with a bound of three tries in all.
answers.reply: > Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: Question 16: The rule for a changed proposal covers only a change after the customer said yes. A customer can also switch to their other open order before saying yes. I propose widening it. Before: "When the customer changes the proposal after saying yes, such as asking to cancel a different order, the earlier yes no longer counts. The agent proposes again and waits for a new yes." After: "When the customer changes the proposal, before or after saying yes, such as asking to cancel a different order, any earlier yes no longer counts. The agent proposes again and waits for a new yes."
answers.recommended: Yes, change the rule to the "After" text.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Proposed default: the agent cancels an order only after the customer explicitly confirms the full proposal (which order, the refund amount and where it goes); any change after confirmation voids it.
> 1. Wrong order cancelled — customer has two open orders and says "cancel my order"; agent must disambiguate and get a confirmation naming the order number before the cancel call.
